faq.q: Is Cambie an official City of Vancouver neighbourhood?
faq.a: No — the City has 22 official local areas and "Cambie" is not one of them; the Cambie Street corridor runs through the official areas of South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge under the Cambie Corridor Plan.

faq.q: What plan governs the Cambie Street corridor?
faq.a: The Cambie Corridor Plan, approved by Council on May 9, 2011, guiding growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River around the Canada Line stations, with Phase 3 (2018) extending policy to the surrounding neighbourhood streets.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve the corridor?
faq.a: Four Canada Line stations: King Edward, Oakridge–41st Avenue, Langara–49th Avenue and Marine Drive.

faq.q: How is this page different from the South Cambie page?
faq.a: South Cambie is one official City local area at the corridor's north end and has its own research file; this Cambie page covers the whole corridor across South Cambie, Riley Park and Oakridge, from West 16th Avenue to Marine Drive.

faq.q: What housing does the corridor plan add?
faq.a: Townhouse and rowhouse areas, low-rise apartments on the surrounding streets under Phase 3, and medium- to higher-density housing at the station areas, anchored by the Oakridge Municipal Town Centre at 41st and Cambie.
